title: Adoption path could render through a ComfyUI launched WITHOUT --reserve-vram (fix applied)
evidence: The --reserve-vram 5 fix (accepted on this board) was bypassable by ADOPTION. bin/comfyui_harness.sh:launch_comfyui adopts any instance already answering :8188 instead of relaunching (queue-first, 2026-09-07), so the launch line is not ours to choose. A co-tenant's un-reserved ComfyUI was live at 2026-09-22 18:43Z (pid 3662070, tmux-spawn scope, args '--listen 0.0.0.0 --enable-manager', 17.1 GiB held, reserve=missing) and cmd_ensure logged 'acquiring claim to adopt it' -- one VRAM condition away from running our two-stage flux workflow at a budget sized to the whole card, i.e. the over-commit that OOMed 78 MiB short at 21.32 GiB allocated on 2026-09-22T00:05Z and then drew HTTP 500 from the broken model state. Measured OOM rate with no reserve, all runs on record: 3/27 renders (09-17), 3/12 (09-17), 6/35 (09-19), 3/3 (09-22 00:0xZ); zero since the flag went on the launch line (02:34Z). Cause sat one layer below the symptom the board tracks (comfyui-torch-oom), so a recurrence would have been attributed to the workflow rather than to the adopted args.

notes.note:
2026-09-22 18:5xZ ops-triage: FIXED IN THE REPO, verified live, no GPU needed. Root cause: adoption chose the launch line for us. Fix (bin/comfyui_harness.sh): (1) new comfyui_reserve_ok [PID] reads the RUNNING instance's /proc/<pid>/cmdline and returns ok only if it carries --reserve-vram -- the args are the discriminator the instrument already trusted at launch time, now applied at adoption time too; (2) cmd_ensure gains the invariant 'never submit a render to a ComfyUI that was not launched with --reserve-vram': it refuses with rc=2 BEFORE requesting a claim (so the refusal costs the window and nothing else -- no job minted, no FIFO entry to cancel, nothing to release), and it fires on the ARGS rather than on ownership, because a launch line that drops the flag must stop the render wherever it came from; (3) the foreign-adoption log line no longer says 'acquiring claim to adopt it' when the flag is missing -- it says NOT adopting it; (4) status now appends reserve=<ok|missing> to the attribution, so a monitor sees the refusal condition before a tick hits it (existing claim=/job=/ours=/comfyui= parse untouched; still exactly one stdout line).

VERIFICATION (real output, no GPU, no claim): (a) bin/comfyui_harness.sh status -> 'claim=idle job=none ours=no comfyui=up owner=foreign pid=3662070 ... reserve=missing' -- the live foreign instance is correctly classified; (b) bin/comfyui_harness_test.sh -> RESULT: ALL PASS, with 8 new assertions on top of the existing 20: reserve ok on flagged argv / missing on unflagged argv / missing for a dead pid (exec -a dummies, no GPU), ensure rc=2 + 'REFUSING this tick' + 'NOT adopting it' + ZERO 'request --gpu' calls under a stub of (comfyui_up=true, ours=false, reserve=false, free=21GiB so only the flag can stop it), and the negative control -- a flagged instance is still adopted and the claim IS requested (so the guard is not a blanket refusal); (c) LIVE: bin/comfyui_harness.sh ensure --wait 180 against the real foreign instance logged 'adaptive fit ... asking 16GiB' -> 'unclaimed FOREIGN ComfyUI (pid 3662070) was launched WITHOUT --reserve-vram -- NOT adopting it' -> 'REFUSING this tick ... no claim requested, nothing to release, no render attempted', rc=2, and /mnt/nas-ai-models/gpu-scheduler/logs/events.log was UNCHANGED before vs after (last entry still the 18:03:43Z cancellation) -- the refusal never touched the scheduler.

BONUS EFFECT, measured in the same live run: the tick no longer mints-then-cancels a queue record while a foreign un-reserved instance holds the card (the 18:00Z tick requested comfyui-1790100041-3823275-1 and cancelled it 3 min later as vram_insufficient; this tick minted nothing), so the FIFO no longer carries our churn.

TRADE, recorded so it is not re-derived: the guard yields the window in the case where the foreign instance holds LITTLE VRAM and the card would otherwise fit us. Accepted, because rendering through an un-reserved instance OOMed at a material rate on every such run on record (above), the OOM also breaks the foreign instance's model state (that is what produced the HTTP 500), and an OOM there would be mis-attributed to our workflow. The alternative -- restarting the co-tenant's instance with the flag -- is forbidden (never interfere with another project's GPU work).
